It's a snap. Very easy to strip and clean. Same with the Remington. I use the 535 for Turkey hunting since it has a threaded barrel for chokes and it's 'camo'd out', so I've had to clean that way more than the 870, which just sits in the corner for home defense. I love both almost equally. They're both fun to take to the range as well.

I bought an H&R Pardner Pump, which is a Remington 870 clone, for that price, and I have absolutely no regrets.

There's something about buying a gun just to beat the crap out of it: I sawed the barrel down to 18", shoot "other" slugs through it, and take it in the woods with my friends -- using it to push brush aside and almost clear paths. It's not an expensive gun, and I don't absolutely need it, so if I break it I'm not out anything -- but it works perfectly well, and I've never had a problem with it.

It's a tool... a cheap tool, but a tool nonetheless. And, being cheap, you don't have to worry about losing anything by getting a few scratches in the barrel or dinging up the stock in any way. It's not like it's a $1K double-barrel, which would make you cry if the finish on the receiver got scratched...

And that's the most appealing thing about it. Hell, if you don't go get it, tell me where it is, and I'll go out there and buy it!
